passage: Students in the town of Belcott stood a stick 1 meter tall straight up in an open schoolyard. On one spring day, they measured the length of its shadow at five different times.

graphic.caption: Shadow of the stick in Belcott on one spring day

prompt: Based on the graph, the shadow at 4 p.m. was how many times as long as the shadow at noon?
explanation: The 4 p.m. bar reaches 1.8 m and the noon bar reaches 0.6 m. 1.8 divided by 0.6 is 3.0, so the 4 p.m. shadow was 3.0 times as long.

distractor_rationales.fault: uses the 10 a.m. bar (1.2 m) instead of the 4 p.m. bar: 1.2 / 0.6
uses the 8 a.m. bar (2.4 m) instead of the 4 p.m. bar: 2.4 / 0.6
divides by the 10 a.m. shadow (1.2 m) instead of the noon shadow: 1.8 / 1.2

real_world_check: A shadow is shortest near midday, when the Sun is highest, and grows longer as the Sun gets lower in the morning and afternoon.
prior_free: Knowing that shadows are shortest near midday gives no size for the change; the comparison of the 4 p.m. and noon shadows exists only in these invented bar heights.

passage: Students at Arbel School tested ways to help a building stay standing during an earthquake. They built four towers from wooden blocks. They kept the number of blocks in each tower at 20. Each tower stood on a different pad: foam, rubber, cork, or bare wood. They wrote the pad material on a card beside each tower. They set each tower on a shake table and kept the table's shaking speed the same for every test. They also kept the length of each shaking test at 30 seconds. After each test, they counted the blocks that fell.
prompt: Which variable did the students change on purpose in this investigation?
choices: the number of blocks in each tower
the length of each shaking test

refs.quote: Each tower stood on a different pad

explanation: Each tower stood on a different pad (foam, rubber, cork or bare wood), so the pad material is what the students changed on purpose. The other three were held the same in every test.

distractor_rationales.fault: the procedure says it stayed the same for every test

distractor_rationales.choice: the number of blocks in each tower
distractor_rationales.fault: it was kept at 20 blocks for every tower

distractor_rationales.choice: the length of each shaking test
distractor_rationales.fault: every shaking test was kept at 30 seconds

real_world_check: In an investigation, the independent variable is the one factor changed on purpose, while the other factors are held the same.

passage: Students studied the rock layers in the wall of a road cut near the town of Efton. The layers are flat and have not been tipped, folded or flipped. The students drew four layers and searched each one for fossils. Layer 1, at the bottom, held fossil shells of clams and sea snails. Layer 2 held fossils of sea stars. Layer 3 held fossil fern leaves and pieces of tree bark. Layer 4, at the top, held rounded river pebbles and no fossils.
prompt: Which claim is NOT supported by what the students observed?
choices: Sea animals lived here before ferns grew in this place.
The fern layer formed before both layers that hold sea fossils.
Land plants grew in this place at one time long ago.
A river ran through this place after the ferns had grown.
correct_answer: The fern layer formed before both layers that hold sea fossils.

refs.quote: Layer 1, at the bottom, held fossil shells

explanation: In flat, unflipped layers, lower layers formed first. The fern fossils are in Layer 3, above both sea-fossil layers (1 and 2), so the fern layer formed later, not earlier. The other three claims match the layers.

distractor_rationales.choice: Sea animals lived here before ferns grew in this place.
distractor_rationales.fault: supported: the sea fossils in Layers 1 and 2 lie below the ferns in Layer 3

distractor_rationales.choice: Land plants grew in this place at one time long ago.
distractor_rationales.fault: supported: Layer 3 holds fern leaves and tree bark, which are land plants

distractor_rationales.choice: A river ran through this place after the ferns had grown.
distractor_rationales.fault: supported: rounded river pebbles in Layer 4 lie above the fern layer

real_world_check: In rock layers that have not been overturned, lower layers formed before the layers above them, and fossils show what lived there at the time.

prompt: Farmers on a wide, open stretch of land plant long rows of trees along the edges of their fields. Strong spring winds blow across the land while the fields are still bare. Which statement best explains how the rows of trees help protect the farmland?
choices: The trees slow the wind near the ground, so it carries off less soil.
The tree roots spread out under the whole field and hold the soil in place.
The trees stop the wind, so the air over the fields stays still.
Fallen leaves become new soil each spring as fast as wind takes it.
correct_answer: The trees slow the wind near the ground, so it carries off less soil.
explanation: A row of trees breaks the wind and slows it near the ground. Slower wind can lift and carry less loose soil off the bare fields, so less soil is lost.

distractor_rationales.choice: The tree roots spread out under the whole field and hold the soil in place.
distractor_rationales.fault: misconception: roots at the field edge anchor the soil across a whole field; they reach only a short way

distractor_rationales.choice: The trees stop the wind, so the air over the fields stays still.
distractor_rationales.fault: misconception: a windbreak stops the wind; it only slows it, and air still moves over the field

distractor_rationales.choice: Fallen leaves become new soil each spring as fast as wind takes it.
distractor_rationales.fault: misconception: soil forms quickly; new soil forms far more slowly than wind can blow it away

real_world_check: Windbreaks of trees reduce wind speed near the ground on their downwind side, which reduces wind erosion of soil.

prompt: On a clear day, a student sees the Sun but no other stars. On a clear night, she sees many stars. Which statement best explains why the other stars are not seen in the daytime?
choices: Stars stop giving off light in the morning, once the Sun comes up in the east.
The Moon covers up the other stars during the day.
Stars move to the far side of the Sun during the daytime.
Sunlight brightens the whole sky, and faint starlight is lost in it.
correct_answer: Sunlight brightens the whole sky, and faint starlight is lost in it.
explanation: The other stars are still in the sky and still shining in the daytime. Sunlight spread across the sky makes it far brighter than the faint light reaching us from those distant stars, so we cannot pick them out.

distractor_rationales.choice: Stars stop giving off light in the morning, once the Sun comes up in the east.
distractor_rationales.fault: misconception: stars shine only at night; they give off light all the time

distractor_rationales.choice: The Moon covers up the other stars during the day.
distractor_rationales.fault: misconception: the Moon hides the stars; the Moon is far too small to cover the sky, and it is often up at night too

distractor_rationales.choice: Stars move to the far side of the Sun during the daytime.
distractor_rationales.fault: misconception: stars travel away in the day; day and night come from Earth spinning, and the stars do not move around the Sun

real_world_check: Stars are above the horizon in daytime too, but sunlight scattered by the air makes the sky much brighter than their light.

passage: Students placed four rock samples, one at a time, in a jar with water and small pebbles. They turned the jar for three days to model rocks tumbling in a fast stream. They weighed each rock before and after.

graphic.caption: Table 1. Rock masses before and after tumbling

prompt: Based on Table 1, how many grams of mass did Sample C-3 lose?
explanation: Sample C-3 had a mass of 150 g before and 133 g after. 150 minus 133 is 17, so it lost 17 g.

distractor_rationales.fault: this is the loss for Sample A-1 (120 - 111), the wrong row
this is the loss for Sample B-2 (120 - 96), the wrong row
subtracts Sample A-1's after mass from Sample C-3's after mass (133 - 111)

real_world_check: Rocks knocked against pebbles in moving water wear down and lose mass, which is a kind of weathering.
prior_free: The standard says moving water and rubbing wear rock down, but not how much any one rock loses; the loss is found only from Sample C-3's two invented masses.

passage: Students built a model of the town of Cadley beside a model river on a long tray. They put a clay wall between the river and the houses. To model a flood, they poured 500 mL of water down the river. They measured how much water got past the wall. They tested walls of four heights.

prompt: The students plan to try a wall 5 cm tall. Based on Table 1, about how much water would most likely get past it?
explanation: A 5 cm wall is halfway between the 4 cm wall (110 mL got past) and the 6 cm wall (70 mL). Halfway between 110 and 70 is 90 mL.

distractor_rationales.fault: this is the 4 cm wall's result; a taller 5 cm wall should let less water past
is halfway between the 2 cm and 4 cm walls, the wrong pair of rows
this is the 6 cm wall's result; a shorter 5 cm wall should let more water past

real_world_check: A taller flood wall holds back more floodwater, so less water gets past it to the houses.
prior_free: Knowing a taller wall holds back more water gives only the direction; the estimate for 5 cm needs the invented 4 cm and 6 cm results.

passage: Students tested how much water four soil samples can hold. They put 300 g of each soil in a cup with small holes in the bottom. They poured 200 mL of water onto each soil, one cup at a time. They caught the water that drained out of the holes and measured it. The water that did not drain out stayed in the soil. Table 1 shows the results.

graphic.caption: Table 1. Water poured onto and drained from four soils

prompt: Based on Table 1, Soil B-4 held how many times as much water as Soil A-6?
explanation: Soil B-4 held 200 - 140 = 60 mL. Soil A-6 held 200 - 180 = 20 mL. 60 divided by 20 is 3.0.

distractor_rationales.fault: divides the water that drained from Soil B-4 (140 mL) by the water Soil A-6 held (20 mL)

prompt: A fast stream flows down a mountain carrying sand and pebbles. Where the stream enters a calm lake, it slows down. The sand and pebbles settle to the lake bottom and slowly build a fan of new land. What is the settling of the sand and pebbles called?
explanation: When moving water slows, it can no longer carry its sand and pebbles, and it drops them. Dropping carried sediment in a new place is deposition.

distractor_rationales.fault: misconception: erosion means any work water does; erosion is picking up and carrying sediment away, not dropping it
misconception: weathering builds land; weathering only breaks rock into smaller pieces where it sits
misconception: all new land is pushed up from below; this land is built by sediment dropped from above

real_world_check: When a stream slows on entering still water, it drops its sediment, and this deposition builds deltas and fans.

prompt: Two stars give off the same amount of light. Seen from Earth, one of them looks much brighter than the other. Which quantity explains why one star looks brighter?
explanation: The two stars give off equal light, so the one that looks brighter must be closer to Earth. A star's light spreads out as it travels, so a nearer star looks brighter.

distractor_rationales.fault: misconception: older stars always look dimmer; how bright a star looks depends on the light it gives off and its distance, and the light is equal here
misconception: stars shine by reflecting sunlight; stars make their own light, so distance from the Sun does not matter
misconception: a wider star always looks brighter; these two give off the same light, so width cannot explain the difference

real_world_check: Two stars that give off the same amount of light look different in brightness from Earth because of their different distances from Earth.

prompt: A town paves over a large grassy field to make a parking lot. A stream runs beside the lot. Which prediction about the water reaching the stream during a heavy rain is correct?
choices: Less water will reach the stream, since pavement soaks up rain like a sponge.
More water will reach the stream, and faster, because rain cannot soak into pavement.
The same amount will reach it, because rain always ends up in the stream.
Less water will reach the stream, since hot pavement dries up rain at once.
correct_answer: More water will reach the stream, and faster, because rain cannot soak into pavement.
explanation: Grass and soil let rain soak into the ground. Pavement is hard and sealed, so the rain runs off across it and reaches the stream faster and in greater amounts.

distractor_rationales.choice: Less water will reach the stream, since pavement soaks up rain like a sponge.
distractor_rationales.fault: misconception: pavement absorbs water; it is sealed, so water runs off it

distractor_rationales.choice: The same amount will reach it, because rain always ends up in the stream.
distractor_rationales.fault: misconception: the ground surface does not matter; soil soaks up much of the rain, but pavement does not

distractor_rationales.choice: Less water will reach the stream, since hot pavement dries up rain at once.
distractor_rationales.fault: misconception: pavement makes heavy rain vanish at once; evaporation during a storm is far too slow

real_world_check: Paved surfaces stop rain from soaking into the ground, which increases the amount and speed of runoff into nearby streams.

graphic.caption: Table 1. Sand blown away from six trays

prompt: A map shows ocean depths along one line. Near the coast, the water is 200 m deep. Farther out, the ocean floor is about 4,000 m deep. Then, beside a curved chain of volcanic islands, a long, narrow strip drops to 10,000 m deep. What is this long, narrow, very deep feature called?
explanation: A long, narrow strip of ocean floor much deeper than the floor around it, lying beside a chain of volcanic islands, is an ocean trench.

distractor_rationales.fault: misconception: the shelf is a deep part of the ocean; it is the shallow edge near the coast, like the 200 m water here
misconception: a seamount is a deep pit; it is an underwater mountain that rises above the ocean floor
misconception: ridges are the deepest places; a mid-ocean ridge is a raised mountain chain, shallower than the floor around it

real_world_check: Ocean trenches are long, narrow, very deep parts of the ocean floor, often found beside chains of volcanic islands.

prompt: At 9 p.m. in January, a student in the northern half of Earth sees a bright group of stars high in the southern sky. She looks for the same group at 9 p.m. in July. Which prediction is correct?
choices: It will be in the same spot, because stars do not move across the sky.
It will look larger, because Earth will be closer to those stars in July.
It will be gone for good, because stars burn out after a few months.
It will be up in the daytime then, so she will not see it.
correct_answer: It will be up in the daytime then, so she will not see it.
explanation: As Earth travels around the Sun, the stars we face at night change with the seasons. By July, the Sun lies in the direction of that star group, so the group is in the sky during the day and cannot be seen at 9 p.m.

distractor_rationales.choice: It will be in the same spot, because stars do not move across the sky.
distractor_rationales.fault: misconception: stars stay fixed in our sky; they appear to move nightly and with the seasons

distractor_rationales.choice: It will look larger, because Earth will be closer to those stars in July.
distractor_rationales.fault: misconception: Earth's orbit brings it noticeably closer to stars; the stars are so far away that the change makes no visible difference

distractor_rationales.choice: It will be gone for good, because stars burn out after a few months.
distractor_rationales.fault: misconception: stars last only months; stars shine for millions to billions of years

real_world_check: Because Earth orbits the Sun, a star group seen high in the evening sky in winter is in the daytime sky six months later.
